tests.title: Real Exam 2026 · Set B · Test 1
tests.topics: Home, friends and hobbies · Reading a book and watching television · A family tradition · Having a hobby

items.question: What do you enjoy most about your home?
items.sample_answer: What I enjoy most about my home is the sense of peace it gives me. After a busy day, I can relax there, be myself, and spend time with my family without any pressure. For me, that comfort matters more than anything else, because home should feel safe, familiar, and welcoming every single day.

items.question: Describe your best friend.
items.sample_answer: My best friend is someone I can completely trust and depend on in difficult moments. He is honest, supportive, and easy to talk to, so I never feel judged around him. We have known each other for years, and that shared history has made our friendship very strong and stable over time.

items.question: What is your favourite hobby?
items.sample_answer: My favourite hobby is reading, because it helps me escape from routine and learn something new at the same time. I especially enjoy books that make me think and stay in my mind after I finish them, and I often recommend them to my friends when I find a really good one.

items.question: What do you see in these pictures?
items.sample_answer: In the first picture, a young man is sitting on a sofa and reading a book in a bright room with a lamp beside him. In the second picture, another man is sitting at home and watching television in a darker living room. Both people are spending their free time indoors, but the first activity looks quieter and more active for the mind, while the second one seems more passive and relaxing.

items.question: What are the advantages of reading a book in your free time?
items.sample_answer: One advantage of reading a book in my free time is that it improves my vocabulary and concentration. It also gives me a break from screens, which I think is healthy, especially after studying or working all day. Another benefit is that books can stay with you longer, because they often make a deeper impression than short videos or online posts.

items.question: Why do most people prefer watching television in the evening?
items.sample_answer: Most people prefer watching television in the evening because it is easy and requires very little effort after a long day. They can sit down, switch it on, and relax without concentrating too much. It is also a simple way to keep up with the news, entertainment, or family programmes while resting at home.

part2.name: Part 2: Cue Card Monologue
part2.topic_question: Describe a tradition that is important in your family or in your region.
card_prompts: Describe a tradition that is important in your family or in your region.
How is this tradition usually celebrated?
Why is it important for young people to keep old traditions alive?
part2.examiner_spoken: Part 2. Describe a tradition that is important in your family or in your region. How is this tradition usually celebrated? Why is it important for young people to keep old traditions alive?
part2.sample_answer:
One tradition that is very important in my family and in my region is celebrating Navruz. It marks the arrival of spring and, for us, it feels like a fresh start after winter. I have always associated it with warmth, kindness, and being together. Even as a child, I understood that this holiday was more than just a day off; it was a meaningful part of our identity and our family life.

Usually, we celebrate it by cleaning the house before the holiday, visiting relatives, and preparing special foods like sumalak and other traditional dishes. In our neighbourhood, there are also concerts, folk games, and people wearing national clothes. Streets become much livelier than usual, and everyone seems to be in a cheerful mood. I remember one Navruz when my family spent the whole day visiting my grandparents, and the atmosphere was so lively that even the children felt part of something meaningful. We laughed, shared food, and talked for hours.

I think it is important for young people to keep old traditions alive because traditions connect us to our history and teach us who we are. They also bring families and communities closer. If young people understand traditions, they can respect their roots while still moving forward in life. Without them, people may lose an important sense of belonging and continuity.

part3.name: Part 3: Two-sided Discussion / Debate
part3.statement: Everyone should have a hobby.
arguments_for: a healthy way to relieve stress after work or study
builds new skills and often new friendships
encourages creativity and personal growth
arguments_against: not everyone has the free time or the money for one
some hobbies are expensive or even risky
a hobby can become an obsession and take over normal life
part3.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Everyone should have a hobby. Use the arguments for and against.
part3.sample_answer:
I partly agree that everyone should have a hobby, because hobbies can make life healthier and more balanced. On the one hand, they are a very good way to relieve stress after work or study. When people do something they enjoy, they can switch off from pressure and feel refreshed. Hobbies also help us develop new skills, and quite often they lead to new friendships. For example, if someone joins a sports club or a language group, they may meet people with similar interests. Another strong point is that hobbies encourage creativity and personal growth, which is important at any age and can make everyday life more satisfying and interesting.

On the other hand, I understand that not everyone has the free time or the money for a hobby. Some activities are expensive, such as photography, travelling, or certain sports, and that can stop people from starting them. Others can even be risky if people do them without proper training or equipment. There is also another danger: a hobby can become an obsession and start controlling a person’s life instead of improving it, especially if someone begins to ignore work, study, or family responsibilities.

In my opinion, having a hobby is highly desirable, but it should be realistic and balanced. Even a simple hobby, like walking, drawing, or reading, can make a big difference if it fits a person’s life and does not create extra problems.

tests.title: Real Exam 2026 · Set B · Test 2
tests.topics: Music, books and evenings · Paper books and electronic books · Time passing quickly or slowly · Standardised testing

items.question: What kind of music do you enjoy listening to?
items.sample_answer: I enjoy listening to calm pop and sometimes instrumental music because it helps me focus, relax, and even improve my mood after a tiring day. If I am studying or walking somewhere, music makes the time pass more pleasantly, so I listen to it quite often. For me, it is one of the easiest ways to switch off mentally.

items.question: Do you have many books at home?
items.sample_answer: Yes, I do. We have quite a lot of books at home, especially school textbooks, novels, and a few old books from my parents and grandparents. I like seeing them on the shelf because they make our home feel more thoughtful, organised, and warm. Even if I do not read every book often, I still value having them around.

items.question: What do you usually do to relax at home?
items.sample_answer: Usually I relax at home by listening to music, watching short videos, or having a cup of tea and talking with my family. If I want something quieter, I read a light book or just lie down and rest for a while. These simple things help me recover after a busy day and feel ready for the next one.

items.question: What do you see in these pictures?
items.sample_answer: In the first picture, a young boy is sitting in a library and reading a printed book very carefully. There are bookshelves full of books behind him, so the place looks quiet and academic. In the second picture, a person is reading an electronic book on a tablet at home or in a comfortable indoor space. Both pictures show people concentrating on reading, but the first one feels more traditional and peaceful, while the second one looks more modern and convenient for everyday use.

items.question: What are the advantages of reading a printed book?
items.sample_answer: One advantage of a printed book is that it is easier on the eyes, especially if you read for a long time. I also like the feeling of turning pages and making notes in the margins, because it makes reading more personal. For me, a real book can create a stronger connection with the story and help me remember it better, so I still prefer paper in many situations.

items.question: Why have electronic books become so popular in recent years?
items.sample_answer: Electronic books have become so popular because they are practical, modern, and very easy to carry around. People can store hundreds of books on one small device and read them anywhere, whether they are travelling, waiting, or relaxing at home. They are also often cheaper than printed books, and that makes them especially attractive for students and busy readers who want quick access.

part2.name: Part 2: Cue Card Monologue
part2.topic_question: Describe a time when the hours passed very quickly, or very slowly.
card_prompts: Describe a time when the hours passed very quickly, or very slowly.
What were you doing and how did you feel?
How important is good time management for a person's success?
part2.examiner_spoken: Part 2. Describe a time when the hours passed very quickly, or very slowly. What were you doing and how did you feel? How important is good time management for a person's success?
part2.sample_answer:
There was a time when the hours passed very slowly for me, and that was during an important exam at school. I had prepared for it for weeks, but once I sat down in the classroom, every minute felt much longer than usual. I kept looking at the clock, and it seemed like the hands were barely moving at all. I was doing my best to stay calm, read each question carefully, and manage my time sensibly so I would not panic.

At first, I felt very nervous because I was afraid of making mistakes and disappointing myself. But after a few minutes, I forced myself to concentrate fully on the task, and that helped me feel a little more confident. I remember telling myself to stop thinking about the time and focus only on the next question. That experience taught me that our feeling of time can change depending on the situation.

On the other hand, I also remember a day when time passed very quickly. It was when I was with my friends at a small picnic outside the city. We were talking, playing games, eating together, and taking photos, and suddenly it was evening. That experience showed me that time management is extremely important for success, because if a person plans their day well, they can study better, avoid stress, and still have time for rest. In my opinion, good time management is not only about being busy; it is about using time wisely and staying focused on what really matters every day.

part3.name: Part 3: Two-sided Discussion / Debate
part3.statement: Standardised tests should be removed from schools.
arguments_for: one exam cannot measure a student's real ability
teachers end up teaching only what will be tested
creates serious stress and anxiety among young people
arguments_against: gives a fair and equal measure for every student
universities and employers need a comparable result
shows which schools and regions need more support
part3.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Standardised tests should be removed from schools. Use the arguments for and against.
part3.sample_answer:
Standardised tests should be removed from schools is a very controversial idea, and I can understand why people argue about it. In my view, there are strong reasons both for and against keeping them.

On the one hand, critics are right to say that one exam cannot show a student’s full ability. Some students are strong in class discussions, creative tasks, or practical work, but they may perform badly when they are under pressure in a test hall. Another problem is that teachers sometimes start teaching only what will appear on the exam, so education becomes too narrow and repetitive. In addition, these tests can create serious stress and anxiety, especially for teenagers who already worry a lot about grades, expectations, and their future.

On the other hand, standardised tests do have clear benefits. They give every student the same conditions, so the result is fair and easier to compare across different schools. Universities and employers also need some kind of common measure when they select people from different places and backgrounds. Besides that, test results can show which schools or regions are falling behind and need more support from the education system.

Personally, I think standardised tests should not be completely removed, but they should be used more carefully and in balance with other forms of assessment. They are useful as one part of education, but they should never be the only thing that decides a student’s future. In a good system, exams would support learning, not control it completely.

items.question: How is your room decorated?
items.sample_answer: My room is fairly simple but comfortable, and I like it that way. I have a desk, a bed, some shelves, and a few family photos on the wall. There is nothing too flashy or crowded in it, because I prefer a calm, uncluttered space where I can relax, study, and feel at home every single day.

items.question: What is your favourite song?
items.sample_answer: My favourite song changes from time to time, but at the moment it is a calm pop song I can listen to while studying or travelling. I like songs with a strong melody and meaningful lyrics because they stay in my head and also improve my mood. Music like that helps me concentrate and feel more positive.

items.question: Do you watch much television?
items.sample_answer: Yes, I do watch television, but not very much, and mostly with a purpose. I usually watch it when there is a news report, an interesting documentary, or a film with my family in the evening. I prefer short, useful programmes rather than spending hours on random shows that do not really interest me much.

items.question: What do you see in these pictures?
items.sample_answer: In the first picture, a young woman is outside taking a selfie with her phone, and she is holding a takeaway drink in the other hand. She seems to be smiling and enjoying herself in a relaxed outdoor setting. In the second picture, a man is sitting indoors while a photographer is taking his portrait with professional equipment. The first scene looks casual, but the second one feels more formal and carefully prepared.

items.question: Why do so many people prefer taking photographs with a phone?
items.sample_answer: I think many people prefer phones because they always have them with them, so taking a photo is quick, simple, and convenient. Also, phone cameras are easy to use, and the pictures can be shared immediately on social media or in messages. For everyday moments, that speed matters more than perfect quality, especially when people want to capture something instantly.

items.question: What can a professional camera do that a phone cannot?
items.sample_answer: A professional camera can usually produce much sharper images and gives the photographer far more control over focus, light, and zoom. It is also better in difficult conditions, such as night photography or a studio setting, where detail really matters. A phone is very handy for daily use, but it cannot fully match that level of quality and flexibility.

part2.name: Part 2: Cue Card Monologue
part2.topic_question: Describe a time when something did not meet your expectations.
card_prompts: Describe a time when something did not meet your expectations.
What had you expected, and what actually happened?
Is it better to have high expectations or low ones?
part2.examiner_spoken: Part 2. Describe a time when something did not meet your expectations. What had you expected, and what actually happened? Is it better to have high expectations or low ones?
part2.sample_answer: A clear example comes from a family trip I took to a mountain resort. Before we went, I expected fresh air, beautiful views, and a quiet place where we could rest properly. I imagined long walks, tasty local food, and a comfortable hotel, so I was really looking forward to it for weeks. In reality, the scenery was beautiful, but the hotel was much smaller and noisier than I had expected, and the weather changed very quickly. It rained heavily on the first day, so some of our plans had to be cancelled. At first I felt disappointed, because I had built the trip up in my mind. However, after a while I realised that the unexpected parts made the experience more memorable. We ended up spending more time together indoors, playing cards, drinking tea, and talking late into the evening. For me, this showed that expectations can shape our feelings a lot. I think it is better to have realistic expectations rather than extremely high or extremely low ones. High expectations can motivate us, but if they are too high, we become disappointed very easily. Low expectations protect us from frustration, but they can also stop us from enjoying life fully. Personally, I try to hope for the best while staying practical and flexible, especially when the situation is outside my control.

part3.statement: Professional athletes are paid far too much money.
arguments_for: their salaries are out of proportion to teachers and doctors
the money could fund grassroots sport for ordinary children
huge pay gives young fans the wrong idea about success
arguments_against: their careers are short and can end with one injury

very few people in the world reach that level of talent
part3.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Professional athletes are paid far too much money. Use the arguments for and against.
part3.sample_answer: The statement is that professional athletes are paid far too much money. I can see why many people think that, and there are strong arguments on both sides. On the one hand, their salaries often seem completely out of proportion when we compare them with the pay of teachers or doctors, who do essential work every single day. People also argue that some of that money could be used to develop grassroots sport for ordinary children, which would benefit society much more in the long run. Another important point is that huge salaries can send the wrong message to young fans, making success look like fame and money rather than hard work, discipline, and character. On the other hand, professional sport is a huge business. Top athletes help bring in enormous income through ticket sales, television rights, sponsorships, and merchandise, so in a sense they earn what the market is willing to pay. Also, their careers are very short, and one serious injury can end everything overnight. Finally, very few people ever reach that level, so the payment reflects how exceptional their talent really is. In my opinion, the salaries are sometimes excessive, but I would not say they are completely unjustified. What bothers me most is not that athletes earn a lot, but that society often fails to value other important professions enough. I think the real issue is balance, not envy or punishment, and that is why I would support a fairer distribution of rewards overall.

Also, phone cameras are easy to use, and the pictures can be shared immediately on social media or in messages. For everyday moments, that speed matters more than perfect quality, especially when people want to capture something instantly.

steps.question: What can a professional camera do that a phone cannot?
steps.examiner_spoken: What can a professional camera do that a phone cannot?
steps.sample_answer: A professional camera can usually produce much sharper images and gives the photographer far more control over focus, light, and zoom. It is also better in difficult conditions, such as night photography or a studio setting, where detail really matters. A phone is very handy for daily use, but it cannot fully match that level of quality and flexibility.

steps.question: Describe a time when something did not meet your expectations.
bullets: Describe a time when something did not meet your expectations.

steps.examiner_spoken: Part 2. Describe a time when something did not meet your expectations. What had you expected, and what actually happened? Is it better to have high expectations or low ones?
steps.sample_answer: A clear example comes from a family trip I took to a mountain resort. Before we went, I expected fresh air, beautiful views, and a quiet place where we could rest properly. I imagined long walks, tasty local food, and a comfortable hotel, so I was really looking forward to it for weeks. In reality, the scenery was beautiful, but the hotel was much smaller and noisier than I had expected, and the weather changed very quickly. It rained heavily on the first day, so some of our plans had to be cancelled. At first I felt disappointed, because I had built the trip up in my mind. However, after a while I realised that the unexpected parts made the experience more memorable. We ended up spending more time together indoors, playing cards, drinking tea, and talking late into the evening. For me, this showed that expectations can shape our feelings a lot. I think it is better to have realistic expectations rather than extremely high or extremely low ones. High expectations can motivate us, but if they are too high, we become disappointed very easily. Low expectations protect us from frustration, but they can also stop us from enjoying life fully. Personally, I try to hope for the best while staying practical and flexible, especially when the situation is outside my control.

steps.question: Professional athletes are paid far too much money.

table.statement: Professional athletes are paid far too much money.

against: their careers are short and can end with one injury

steps.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Professional athletes are paid far too much money. Use the arguments for and against.
steps.sample_answer: The statement is that professional athletes are paid far too much money. I can see why many people think that, and there are strong arguments on both sides. On the one hand, their salaries often seem completely out of proportion when we compare them with the pay of teachers or doctors, who do essential work every single day. People also argue that some of that money could be used to develop grassroots sport for ordinary children, which would benefit society much more in the long run. Another important point is that huge salaries can send the wrong message to young fans, making success look like fame and money rather than hard work, discipline, and character. On the other hand, professional sport is a huge business. Top athletes help bring in enormous income through ticket sales, television rights, sponsorships, and merchandise, so in a sense they earn what the market is willing to pay. Also, their careers are very short, and one serious injury can end everything overnight. Finally, very few people ever reach that level, so the payment reflects how exceptional their talent really is. In my opinion, the salaries are sometimes excessive, but I would not say they are completely unjustified. What bothers me most is not that athletes earn a lot, but that society often fails to value other important professions enough. I think the real issue is balance, not envy or punishment, and that is why I would support a fairer distribution of rewards overall.

part2.sample_answer:
One time when I worked as part of a team was during a school project in my final year. We had to prepare a presentation about how to improve life in our city, and the teacher asked us to work in groups of four. At first, we were a bit disorganised because everyone had ideas, but no clear plan. Then we divided the work and started helping each other properly.

My own role in the team was to organise the material and make sure our presentation had a clear structure. I also researched some statistics and helped turn our notes into simple, natural English. Another student designed the slides, and the other two practised speaking parts. I think my strength was keeping everything on track and checking that we finished on time. I remember one evening we stayed after class to correct mistakes together, and that made the whole project much stronger.

The biggest benefit of working together is that you can combine different skills and finish a task more effectively. One person may be creative, another may be good at speaking, and another may be strong with details. Also, when people support each other, the pressure feels smaller. In my experience, a team can produce a much better result than one person working alone, especially when there is a lot to do.

part3.name: Part 3: Two-sided Discussion / Debate
part3.statement: The number of tourists allowed into historical cities should be limited.
arguments_for: protects fragile monuments from damage and overcrowding
improves daily life for the people who live there
a calmer visit is a better experience for the tourist too
arguments_against: tourism is a major source of income and local jobs
everyone has the right to see their own cultural heritage
the money from visitors pays for restoration work
part3.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: The number of tourists allowed into historical cities should be limited. Use the arguments for and against.
part3.sample_answer:
I think the idea of limiting the number of tourists in historical cities is understandable, but it should not be done too strictly. On the one hand, I agree that these places need protection. Old monuments are fragile, and too many visitors can damage streets, buildings, and the overall atmosphere. Crowds also make daily life harder for local residents, and the city becomes less enjoyable for everyone. In fact, a calmer visit often gives tourists a better experience because they can actually appreciate the place instead of rushing through it.

On the other hand, tourism brings real benefits. In many historical cities, it is a major source of income and creates jobs for guides, hotel workers, shop owners, and restaurant staff. I also think people should have the chance to see and enjoy cultural heritage, not just locals. What is more, the money tourists spend can be used to restore monuments and maintain public spaces, which is extremely important for preservation. Without that income, many beautiful places would struggle to survive.

So, my opinion is that cities should control numbers in a smart way rather than simply closing themselves off. For example, they can use timed tickets, protect the busiest sites, and encourage visitors to come in less crowded seasons. That seems to me like the best balance between preservation and access, and it respects both the city and the people who want to visit it. In other words, the goal should be sustainable tourism, not a total ban.

items.question: Describe your family.
items.sample_answer: I’d say my family is quite close-knit and supportive. There are four of us: my parents, my younger sister and me. We don’t always agree on everything, but we usually solve problems by talking calmly and listening to each other, and that makes home feel safe, relaxed, and comfortable for everyone.

items.question: Tell me about the nicest place you have ever visited.
items.sample_answer: The nicest place I’ve ever visited was probably a quiet mountain area with fresh air, green views, and a very peaceful atmosphere. I liked it because it was completely different from my usual routine, so I could switch off, enjoy the scenery, take a lot of photos, and really relax for a while.

items.question: What do you usually do with your family at the weekend?
items.sample_answer: At the weekend, I usually spend time with my family at home or go out together for a meal or a short walk. I think these simple moments matter most, because they help us stay connected, share small news, laugh together, and enjoy each other’s company even when weekdays are busy.

items.question: What do you see in these pictures?
items.sample_answer: In the first picture, I can see a woman sitting on a balcony surrounded by many potted plants and flowers, and she seems to be enjoying a drink while looking out over the garden below. In the second picture, there is a family sitting together at a dining table in a kitchen, eating a meal and smiling. Both pictures show calm, homely moments, but the first one feels more private and quiet, while the second one is warmer, busier, and more social.

items.question: What are the advantages of living in a house with a garden?
items.sample_answer: One advantage of living in a house with a garden is that you have more space and fresh air around you. You can relax outside, grow plants, have a barbecue, or let children play safely. I think a garden also makes a home feel more peaceful and pleasant, especially if you spend a lot of time indoors during the week.

items.question: Why do so many people choose to live in a flat in the city?
items.sample_answer: Many people choose to live in a flat in the city because it is practical and convenient for everyday life. Flats are often closer to work, schools, shops, cafés, and public transport, so people can save time and money. For busy people, that convenience often matters more than having a large amount of space, a quiet garden, or extra rooms.

part2.name: Part 2: Cue Card Monologue
part2.topic_question: Describe a time when you did something important completely on your own.
card_prompts: Describe a time when you did something important completely on your own.
How did you feel while you were doing it?
At what age should young people start becoming independent?
part2.examiner_spoken: Part 2. Describe a time when you did something important completely on your own. How did you feel while you were doing it? At what age should young people start becoming independent?
part2.sample_answer:
A few years ago, I organised a small charity event at my school completely on my own. We wanted to raise money for children who needed books, so I decided to plan everything myself instead of waiting for other people. I made posters, spoke to teachers, collected donations, and arranged a small table where students could buy cakes and drinks. It was the first time I had taken responsibility for such a big task without asking someone else to do it for me.

While I was doing it, I felt nervous at first because I was afraid something might go wrong. I worried that nobody would support the idea or that I would forget something important. However, as more people became interested and started helping, I became much more confident and proud of myself. By the end of the day, I felt tired but very satisfied, because I could clearly see that my effort had made a real difference.

That experience taught me that I can manage difficult things if I stay organised, calm, and focused. In my opinion, young people should start becoming independent quite early, but in small steps rather than all at once. Around 14 or 15 is a good age to begin taking more responsibility, such as managing money, helping at home, or solving simple problems alone. If teenagers learn independence gradually, they are much more likely to become confident adults later on.

part3.name: Part 3: Two-sided Discussion / Debate
part3.statement: Space tourism should be banned.
arguments_for: every flight releases an enormous amount of pollution
the money would do more good solving problems on Earth
it is a luxury only the very richest people can buy
arguments_against: private spending speeds up space technology for everyone
it creates highly skilled jobs and whole new industries
exploration has always pushed human knowledge forward
part3.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Space tourism should be banned. Use the arguments for and against.
part3.sample_answer:
I think this is a difficult issue, because space tourism has both serious disadvantages and some possible benefits. On the one hand, I understand why people want it banned. Every flight creates a huge amount of pollution, and that is hard to justify when we already have so many environmental problems on Earth. Also, the money spent on luxury trips into space could be used to fight poverty, improve education, build hospitals, or support scientific research that helps ordinary people directly. And honestly, at the moment, this is mostly entertainment for the very richest people, not something ordinary citizens can enjoy.

On the other hand, I don’t think a complete ban is the best solution. Private investment often pushes technology forward much faster than governments can do alone, because companies compete to make things safer, cheaper, and more efficient. What starts as an expensive luxury can later become useful for everyone, just like many modern technologies did in the past. It also creates highly skilled jobs and supports new industries in engineering, science, manufacturing, and tourism. More importantly, exploration has always helped humanity learn more about the universe and about our own planet.

My own view is that space tourism should not be banned, but it should be tightly controlled and limited. Companies should be required to reduce emissions as much as possible, and part of their profits could support environmental or scientific projects on Earth. In that way, we can protect the planet without stopping progress completely.

items.question: Describe your home.

It isn’t very large, but it feels warm and welcoming because my family has made it our own with books, plants, simple furniture, and a lot of personal touches. I like it because it is peaceful and easy to relax in after a busy day.

items.question: Do you have any pets?
items.sample_answer: Yes, I do have pets. I have a cat, and I really enjoy looking after him because he is calm, funny, and easy to be around, especially when I’m tired after a long day. He also gives the house a more lively feeling, and I think pets make daily life less stressful and more enjoyable.

items.question: What is your favourite meal of the day?
items.sample_answer: My favourite meal of the day is dinner, because that is when my family usually sits together and talks about our day. I also like it because I can eat slowly and relax after school or work, instead of rushing. For me, dinner feels like both a meal and a chance to connect with people.

items.question: What do you see in these pictures?

In the second picture, two women are sitting face to face and having a friendly conversation indoors. The main difference is that the first person is communicating by phone, while the second scene shows direct personal contact and a much warmer, more personal kind of communication.

items.question: What are the advantages of talking to someone face to face?
items.sample_answer: One clear advantage of talking face to face is that I can understand the other person much better. I can see their facial expressions, gestures, and tone of voice, so the conversation feels warmer and more natural. It also helps avoid misunderstandings, because if something is unclear, I can react immediately, ask another question, and explain myself properly. That makes the whole exchange easier and often more honest.

items.question: Why do people often prefer to call or message instead?
items.sample_answer: People often prefer to call or message instead because it is faster and more convenient in daily life. They may be busy, travelling, or simply unable to meet in person. Also, messages give people time to think before answering, which can be useful if the topic is serious or emotional, and it sometimes feels easier to write than to speak directly, especially when people are shy.

She told me to stop trying to revise everything at once and instead make a simple daily plan with short sessions and regular breaks. That sounded basic, but it changed my routine completely. Before that, I used to study for hours without a clear order, and I often ended up feeling tired and confused.

I trusted her because she was experienced and had seen many students make the same mistake. part3.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Video games are beneficial for young people. Use the arguments for and against.
part3.sample_answer:
I think the statement that video games are beneficial for young people is partly true, but it depends very much on how they are used. On the one hand, many games can improve reaction speed, memory, and problem-solving skills, because players have to think quickly and make decisions under pressure. In strategy or adventure games, for example, you often have to remember rules, plan several moves ahead, and adapt when something goes wrong. Also, a lot of games are team-based, so they can teach cooperation, communication, and even leadership. If friends play together online, they also have a shared activity and a reason to stay in touch. Another point is that gaming can be a cheap and social way to relax, especially for teenagers who cannot always afford other hobbies or entertainment.

On the other hand, there are serious drawbacks. Long hours in front of a screen can damage health and sleep, especially if young people play late at night and then wake up tired the next morning. Games can also take time away from study, exercise, and real friendships, which are all important for healthy development. In addition, some games are violent, and some are clearly designed to be addictive, so players may find it hard to stop even when they know they should.

Overall, I would say video games are beneficial only when they are balanced and limited. Used sensibly, they can be entertaining and even educational, but they should never replace real life activities or the responsibilities that young people need to develop.

tests.topics: Neighbourhood, friends and evenings · Studying alone and studying in a group · Setting yourself a goal · Teaching handwriting

items.question: Can you describe the area where you live?
items.sample_answer: Yes, I live in a fairly quiet residential area on the edge of the city. There are apartment blocks, small shops, and a park nearby, so it feels comfortable and practical. I like it because everything I need is within walking distance, but it is still peaceful enough to relax in the evenings after a busy day.

items.question: Who is your closest friend and why?
items.sample_answer: My closest friend is someone I have known since school, and I trust him completely. What makes him special is that he is honest, reliable, and easy to talk to. Even when we disagree, he listens carefully, gives sensible advice, and never judges me, which is rare and valuable.

items.question: How do you usually spend your evenings?
items.sample_answer: I usually spend my evenings finishing my homework, helping at home, and then relaxing a bit. If I have energy left, I watch a short video, read, or go for a walk around my neighbourhood. I like keeping my evenings balanced, because it helps me stay productive without feeling exhausted later.

items.question: What do you see in these pictures?
items.sample_answer: In the first picture, I see a man sitting alone at a desk and writing in a notebook. There is a large computer beside him, but he seems to be focusing on his handwritten work instead of the screen. In the second picture, several people are sitting closely together around a table and discussing something. So the main difference is that one scene shows individual study, while the other shows group learning and collaboration.

items.question: What are the advantages of studying on your own?
items.sample_answer: Studying on your own has several advantages. First, you can learn at your own speed and spend more time on difficult topics without feeling embarrassed. Second, you do not depend on other people’s schedules, which makes it much more flexible and convenient. I also think it helps you become more independent and responsible, because you have to organise your own work and solve problems by yourself.

items.question: Why do many students learn better in a group?
items.sample_answer: Many students learn better in a group because they can share ideas and explain things to one another in simple language. If one person does not understand something, another can give a clear explanation or a useful example. Group study also makes people more motivated, because working with others can be more active and less boring. For some learners, that social energy really improves concentration and results.

part2.name: Part 2: Cue Card Monologue
part2.topic_question: Describe an ambitious goal that you set for yourself.
card_prompts: Describe an ambitious goal that you set for yourself.
How did it affect your personal and your professional life?
Are there any drawbacks to being a very ambitious person?
part2.examiner_spoken: Part 2. Describe an ambitious goal that you set for yourself. How did it affect your personal and your professional life? Are there any drawbacks to being a very ambitious person?
part2.sample_answer: One ambitious goal I set for myself was to improve my English enough to speak confidently in public and use it for study and work. I decided on this goal because I realised that English could open many doors for me, especially in education and career opportunities. At first, it felt quite challenging, but I made a clear plan and tried to practise a little every day. I watched videos, read short articles, learned new vocabulary, and spoke even when I made mistakes. Over time, that ambition changed both my personal and professional life in very positive ways. Personally, I became more disciplined, more patient, and much more confident in myself. I stopped being afraid of difficult tasks, because I had proof that steady effort really works. Professionally, my English improved my communication skills and made me more interested in international opportunities and future jobs. It also helped me understand that ambition is useful when it pushes you to grow rather than just to compete with other people. Of course, there are drawbacks to being very ambitious. Sometimes ambitious people become too stressed, impatient, or disappointed if progress is slower than expected. They can also forget to rest or enjoy the present moment. So I think ambition is a great quality, but only if it is balanced with patience, self-care, and realistic expectations.

part3.name: Part 3: Two-sided Discussion / Debate
part3.statement: Handwriting should still be taught in schools.
arguments_for: writing by hand helps children remember what they learn
develops fine motor control and concentration
pen and paper always work, with no battery or signal
arguments_against: almost all adult work is now done on a keyboard
those hours could be spent on digital skills instead
typing is faster and far easier for everyone to read
part3.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Handwriting should still be taught in schools. Use the arguments for and against.
part3.sample_answer: The statement is that handwriting should still be taught in schools, and I mostly agree with it. On the one hand, writing by hand can help children remember information better, because the process is slower and more active than typing. It also develops fine motor control and concentration, which are useful skills for young learners in many other subjects too. Another practical advantage is that pen and paper always work, even when there is no battery, internet connection, or signal, so they are reliable in any situation. On the other hand, there are strong arguments against spending too much time on handwriting. In adult life, almost all work is done on keyboards, so schools should prepare students for that reality and give more space to digital skills. Also, those lesson hours could be used for learning technology, which is increasingly important in education and employment. And to be honest, typing is usually faster and much easier for other people to read, which saves time and avoids confusion. In my opinion, handwriting should not disappear completely, but it should be taught in a balanced way. I think young students need enough practice to write clearly and confidently, but schools should not treat it as more important than digital literacy. A modern education should give children both skills, because they will need both in different parts of life.

tests.title: Real Exam 2026 · Set B · Test 8
tests.topics: Room, health and routine · How older and younger people spend time · Forgiving someone · Keeping pets

items.question: Tell me about your room.
items.sample_answer: I’d say my room is quite simple but comfortable. I have a bed, a desk and a bookshelf, and I usually keep it tidy because I can think better in a clean space. I also like having a few photos and small things that make it feel personal, so it doesn’t look too empty. It’s the place where I study, relax and switch off after a long day.

items.question: What do you do to stay healthy?
items.sample_answer: To stay healthy, I try to eat balanced food, drink enough water and move around every day. I don’t always do intense exercise, but I walk a lot and sometimes do a short workout at home. I think regular habits matter more than doing something extreme once in a while, because small choices every day really add up.

items.question: Do you usually get up early or late?
items.sample_answer: I usually get up early on weekdays because I have school or other responsibilities. On weekends I tend to wake up later, especially if I’ve had a busy week. For me, early mornings are better for work, but I also enjoy a slower start when I have free time. If I sleep well, I can concentrate much better during the day.

items.question: What do you see in these pictures?
items.sample_answer: In the first picture, I can see a group of adults sitting around a table and playing cards. They look relaxed and happy, and the atmosphere seems very friendly. In the second picture, there are several young people sitting outside, probably on a campus, chatting and using a phone or reading. The first group looks like older people spending time together indoors, while the second group seems younger and more casual outdoors, so the mood and setting are quite different.

items.question: How do older and younger people spend their free time differently?
items.sample_answer: Older and younger people often spend their free time differently because their interests and energy levels are not the same. Younger people usually prefer social media, sports or hanging out with friends, while older people may enjoy quieter activities like chatting, playing games or taking a walk. Of course, there is overlap, but the younger group is often more active and digital, whereas older people tend to choose calmer leisure, especially when they want to relax after work.

items.question: What can younger people learn from spending time with older people?
items.sample_answer: Younger people can learn a lot from older people, especially patience, life experience and the ability to see problems in a calmer way. Older people often know how to handle difficulties because they have already been through many situations. I also think younger people can learn respect and communication from them. Just talking regularly with older people can give you useful advice for real life, and sometimes one simple conversation can change your view completely.

part2.name: Part 2: Cue Card Monologue
part2.topic_question: Describe a time when you forgave someone, or someone forgave you.
card_prompts: Describe a time when you forgave someone, or someone forgave you.
What had happened between you?
Why is forgiveness important in a family or a friendship?
part2.examiner_spoken: Part 2. Describe a time when you forgave someone, or someone forgave you. What had happened between you? Why is forgiveness important in a family or a friendship?
part2.sample_answer:
I remember a time when I forgave my close friend after a serious misunderstanding. We had planned to prepare a school project together, but at the last minute he didn’t show up and didn’t answer my messages. I was angry because I thought he had ignored me on purpose, and I finished the work alone. I honestly felt disappointed and a little embarrassed, because I had trusted him completely and expected him to be there.

A few days later, he explained that his father had taken him to another city because of a family emergency, and his phone battery had died. He was really upset, and I could see that he had not meant to let me down. What helped me forgive him was his honesty and the fact that he apologised sincerely. He didn’t make excuses; he simply told me the truth, and that made a big difference.

I realised that if I held onto my anger, our friendship would only become weaker. In the end, I told him that I understood and that we could move on. I think forgiveness is very important in a family or a friendship because nobody is perfect. People make mistakes, sometimes without meaning to hurt us. If you forgive, you protect trust and create a chance to start again. Of course, forgiveness doesn’t mean pretending nothing happened, but it does mean choosing the relationship over resentment.

part3.statement: Keeping a pet improves a person's quality of life.

arguments_against: pets cost money and need daily time and attention

part3.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Keeping a pet improves a person's quality of life. Use the arguments for and against.
part3.sample_answer:
I agree with the idea that keeping a pet improves a person’s quality of life, although I think it depends on the situation. On the one hand, pets give companionship and emotional support. For someone who lives alone, a dog or even a cat can make the home feel warmer and less lonely. They are often good listeners in their own way, and just being around an animal can reduce stress. Pets also teach responsibility, because you have to feed them, clean up after them and keep a routine. In addition, dog owners usually walk more, so they become more active without even planning a workout.

On the other hand, pets are not always practical. They cost money for food, vet visits and other care, and they need daily attention. If a person is very busy or lives in a small flat, it can be difficult to give an animal enough space and time. Also, although people don’t always think about it, losing a pet can be genuinely painful and can stay with you for a long time. That emotional cost is real and should not be ignored.

For me, the benefits are stronger than the disadvantages if someone is prepared. I think a pet can improve daily life a lot, but only when the owner is ready for the responsibility and understands that caring for an animal is a long-term commitment. In other words, a pet is not just a hobby; it becomes part of the family.

teaches responsibility, routine and patience
owners walk more and are generally more active
against: pets cost money and need daily time and attention
unsuitable for small flats or very busy households
losing a pet causes genuine and lasting distress

steps.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Keeping a pet improves a person's quality of life. Use the arguments for and against.
steps.sample_answer:
I agree with the idea that keeping a pet improves a person’s quality of life, although I think it depends on the situation. On the one hand, pets give companionship and emotional support. For someone who lives alone, a dog or even a cat can make the home feel warmer and less lonely. They are often good listeners in their own way, and just being around an animal can reduce stress. Pets also teach responsibility, because you have to feed them, clean up after them and keep a routine. In addition, dog owners usually walk more, so they become more active without even planning a workout.

On the other hand, pets are not always practical. They cost money for food, vet visits and other care, and they need daily attention. If a person is very busy or lives in a small flat, it can be difficult to give an animal enough space and time. Also, although people don’t always think about it, losing a pet can be genuinely painful and can stay with you for a long time. That emotional cost is real and should not be ignored.

For me, the benefits are stronger than the disadvantages if someone is prepared. I think a pet can improve daily life a lot, but only when the owner is ready for the responsibility and understands that caring for an animal is a long-term commitment. In other words, a pet is not just a hobby; it becomes part of the family.

tests.title: Real Exam 2026 · Set B · Test 9
tests.topics: Family time, home and food · Free time alone and with other people · A regret you have · Animals in zoos

items.question: Do you usually spend much time with your family?
items.sample_answer: Yes, I do, especially in the evenings and at weekends. We try to have dinner together or just talk about our day, because that helps us stay close even when we are all busy. I think those little conversations are important, since they make family life feel supportive and warm, not just routine. In a fast-paced life, that regular contact really matters to me.

items.question: Describe your bedroom.
items.sample_answer: My bedroom is quite simple and comfortable. I have a bed, a desk, a wardrobe and a small bookshelf, and I like it because it feels calm and private, which helps me relax after a long day. I also keep it tidy most of the time, because I focus much better when everything has its place and the room does not feel crowded.

items.question: What is your favourite dish?
items.sample_answer: My favourite dish is plov, because it is filling and has a rich flavour. I especially enjoy it when it is cooked at family gatherings, since the smell and the atmosphere make it taste even better. It also reminds me of celebrations, so it feels special, not just delicious. For me, it is one of those meals that always feels like home.

items.question: What do you see in these pictures?
items.sample_answer: In the first picture, I can see a woman sitting alone on a bench in a park by the water. It looks peaceful and autumnal, with trees around her and fallen leaves on the ground. In the second picture, a group of friends is in a cinema, laughing and eating popcorn while watching a film. The main difference is that the first person is spending free time quietly on her own, whereas the second group is enjoying a lively shared experience.

items.question: What are the advantages of spending free time on your own?
items.sample_answer: One advantage is that you can do exactly what you want without needing to compromise with anyone. You can read, think, listen to music or just rest in silence, which is often the best way to recharge. It can also help you understand yourself better, because alone time gives you space to reflect on your thoughts and feelings. For me, that kind of quiet time is sometimes the fastest way to recover after a busy week.

items.question: Why do most people prefer to relax with friends or family?
items.sample_answer: Most people prefer to relax with friends or family because it feels more enjoyable and emotionally warm. When you share free time with people you care about, you can talk, laugh and create memories together. Also, many activities are simply more fun in company, and being around others can make people feel less stressed and less lonely. That social connection is one of the main reasons people choose company over being alone, especially after a difficult day.

part2.name: Part 2: Cue Card Monologue
part2.topic_question: Describe something in your life that you regret.
card_prompts: Describe something in your life that you regret.
What would you do differently if you could go back?
Can regret ever have a positive effect on a person?
part2.examiner_spoken: Part 2. Describe something in your life that you regret. What would you do differently if you could go back? Can regret ever have a positive effect on a person?
part2.sample_answer: One thing I regret is not taking my studies seriously enough when I was younger. I used to think there would always be time to catch up, so I sometimes wasted days on unimportant things instead of building good habits. Later, I realised that those missed opportunities were hard to recover, especially when deadlines and exams started to pile up. If I could go back, I would organise my time better, ask for help earlier, and be more disciplined from the beginning. I would also try to worry less about being perfect and focus more on steady progress, because even small steps matter. I think regret can have a positive effect if a person learns from it instead of just feeling bad. For example, regret can push you to change your behaviour, become more responsible, and value your chances more carefully. In my case, regretting wasted time taught me to respect deadlines and to treat every small effort as something important. So although regret is uncomfortable, it can be a useful teacher if we are honest with ourselves and actually act on what we have learned. It may even motivate us to avoid making the same mistake twice, which is why I do not see regret as completely negative.

part3.name: Part 3: Two-sided Discussion / Debate
part3.statement: Animals should be kept in their natural habitat, not in zoos.
arguments_for: animals live freely and behave naturally in the wild
captivity causes stress and unnatural behaviour
it respects animal rights and prevents mistreatment
arguments_against: zoos protect and breed endangered species
they teach the public to care about wildlife
scientists can study animals closely and safely
part3.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Animals should be kept in their natural habitat, not in zoos. Use the arguments for and against.
part3.sample_answer: The statement says that animals should be kept in their natural habitat, not in zoos. I partly agree with this idea, because there are strong arguments on both sides, and the issue is more complicated than it first appears. On the one hand, animals in the wild can live more freely and behave in ways that are natural to them. They can move over large areas, hunt, socialise and follow their instincts. In zoos, by contrast, many animals experience stress, boredom or strange behaviour because their environment is limited and artificial. From an ethical point of view, keeping animals in captivity can also seem like a form of control that ignores their rights and may lead to mistreatment if conditions are poor or overcrowded. On the other hand, zoos can play an important role in protecting endangered species. Some animals survive today because breeding programmes in captivity have saved them from extinction, and without that help their numbers might have disappeared completely. Zoos also educate the public and can make people care more about wildlife and conservation, especially children who may never see these animals otherwise. In addition, scientists can study animals closely in zoos, which may help them improve protection in the wild and learn more about behaviour and health. Personally, I believe wild habitats are always better for animals, but I think zoos can be justified only when they are truly focused on conservation, education and humane care. They should never exist just for entertainment, because animals are not there for our amusement.

tests.title: Real Exam 2026 · Set B · Test 10
tests.topics: School, routine and weather · Traditional and modern classrooms · Feeling confident in yourself · Online privacy

items.question: Describe your school or your workplace.
items.sample_answer: I’d describe my school as a busy but friendly place where students are encouraged to work hard, ask questions and support one another. We have modern classrooms, a small library and teachers who are usually supportive and patient. I like it because the atmosphere is positive, so it is easier to stay motivated, improve and feel confident.

items.question: What time do you usually wake up?
items.sample_answer: I usually wake up at around 7 a.m. on weekdays because that gives me enough time to get ready calmly and have breakfast before I start my day. If I wake up too late, I feel rushed and unsettled, and that makes it harder to concentrate properly during the morning lessons.

items.question: What is the weather like today?
items.sample_answer: Today the weather looks fairly mild and pleasant, though it seems a bit cloudy. I’d probably call it comfortable rather than hot or cold, so it feels quite easy to go outside. Weather like this is actually nice because it makes studying, travelling or walking around much more comfortable.

items.question: What do you see in these pictures?
items.sample_answer: In the first picture, I can see a teacher standing in front of a few students in a modern classroom. The room is bright and tidy, with bookshelves, plants and separate desks for each student. In the second picture, there is a more traditional classroom where the teacher is at the front and several children are raising their hands. Both pictures show learning, but the first one looks more flexible and open, while the second feels more formal and structured.

items.question: What are the advantages of a modern, flexible classroom?
items.sample_answer: A modern, flexible classroom has a lot of advantages for both students and teachers. It usually feels brighter, more comfortable and less restrictive than a traditional room. The furniture can be moved around, so it is easier to work in pairs or groups, or even do different activities during one lesson. I think that kind of space encourages creativity, movement and participation, so students often feel more engaged and confident.

items.question: Why do many teachers still prefer a traditional classroom?
items.sample_answer: Many teachers still prefer a traditional classroom because it is easier to control and organise. When all the desks face the teacher, it is simpler for students to focus on the explanation, especially during a grammar lesson or a test. It also creates a clear sense of order and discipline, which can be very useful. For some subjects, and for younger learners too, that familiar structure works really well.

part2.name: Part 2: Cue Card Monologue
part2.topic_question: Describe a time when you felt truly confident in yourself.
card_prompts: Describe a time when you felt truly confident in yourself.
What had given you that confidence?
How can a person build real self-confidence?
part2.examiner_spoken: Part 2. Describe a time when you felt truly confident in yourself. What had given you that confidence? How can a person build real self-confidence?
part2.sample_answer:
I felt truly confident in myself when I gave a short presentation in English at school last year. I still remember that day clearly because I had always been nervous about speaking in front of other people. Before the lesson, I prepared carefully, practised my words at home several times and tried to imagine the questions my classmates might ask. I also wrote a few key ideas on small notes, just in case I forgot something. When I stood up and started speaking, I was afraid at first, but after the first minute I relaxed a little. I noticed that people were listening attentively and some of them were even nodding, which encouraged me more. By the end of the presentation, I answered the teacher’s questions without hesitation, and that made me feel proud of myself.

What gave me that confidence was a combination of preparation and support. I knew my topic well, so I was not completely guessing, and one of my close friends had encouraged me before the lesson, which helped calm my nerves. Also, I had improved my English gradually over time, so I could actually see progress in myself instead of just hoping to do well.

I think a person builds real self-confidence by setting small goals and achieving them step by step. It also helps to learn from mistakes instead of being ashamed of them. When people practise regularly, accept feedback and remind themselves of their strengths, confidence grows naturally and becomes much more stable and real.

part3.name: Part 3: Two-sided Discussion / Debate
part3.statement: Online privacy is more important than national security.
arguments_for: privacy is a basic right of every citizen
collected data can be leaked, stolen or misused
mass surveillance rarely stops serious crime
arguments_against: monitoring helps prevent terrorism and organised crime
online data protects children from exploitation
honest people lose very little by being checked
part3.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Online privacy is more important than national security. Use the arguments for and against.
part3.sample_answer:
This statement is very relevant today because almost everything we do online leaves some kind of digital trace. On the one hand, online privacy is a basic right, and people should not feel constantly watched just because they use the internet. Our personal data can be leaked, stolen or misused by companies or criminals, and once that happens, the damage can be long-lasting. Supporters of privacy also argue that mass surveillance rarely stops serious crime, because determined criminals often find ways around it.

On the other hand, people who support security say that monitoring can help prevent terrorism and organised crime before innocent people are harmed. It can also protect children from exploitation online, which is a very serious issue. In addition, some people believe that honest citizens lose very little if their activity is checked, especially when the aim is public safety.

Personally, I think privacy should be the priority, but not in an absolute sense. Governments need to collect some data, but only with clear rules, strong legal control and real transparency. If surveillance becomes too broad, it can damage trust and create more risks than it solves. So I support limited monitoring, but only when it is necessary and carefully controlled.

tests.title: Real Exam 2026 · Set A · Test 1
tests.topics: Home and evenings · Healthy food and fast food · Sharing a secret · Calorie information in restaurants

items.question: Do you live in a house or in a flat?
items.sample_answer: I live in a flat at the moment, and although it is not very spacious, I really like it because it is practical, easy to clean, and perfectly suitable for my daily routine and the way I live now.

items.question: What do you usually do in the evening?
items.sample_answer: In the evening, I usually relax after work or study, have dinner, and then spend some time on my phone, reading messages, watching a series, or just doing a bit of nothing to switch off properly.

items.question: Do you like cooking?
items.sample_answer: Yes, I do enjoy cooking, especially simple home-style meals. I’m not an expert, but I like it because it helps me relax, and I also feel more in control of what I eat and how healthy it is.

items.question: What do you see in these pictures?
items.sample_answer: In the first picture, I can see a woman sitting at a table and preparing a fresh salad. There are lots of fruits and vegetables around her, including bananas, oranges, broccoli, and other healthy-looking food. In the second picture, there is a man eating fast food, such as burgers, fries, doughnuts, and fried chicken. The contrast is very strong: one image suggests a balanced lifestyle, while the other shows overeating and much less healthy food.

items.question: What is the biggest difficulty people face in keeping to a healthy diet?
items.sample_answer: I think the biggest difficulty is self-control, because most people already know what they should eat, but they often choose convenience instead. Fast food is quick, cheap, and tasty, so when people are busy, tired, or stressed, they find it hard to say no. Another problem is habit: once someone gets used to unhealthy food, it becomes difficult to change their routine.

items.question: How can we encourage more people to eat healthy food?
items.sample_answer: I think we can encourage healthy eating by making it easier and more attractive. For example, healthy food should be available everywhere, and it should not cost much more than junk food. Schools and workplaces could also promote balanced meals, and social media campaigns could show that healthy food can be tasty, simple, and satisfying rather than boring and unrealistic.

part2.name: Part 2: Cue Card Monologue
part2.topic_question: Describe a time when you shared a secret with someone.
card_prompts: Describe a time when you shared a secret with someone.
Why did you decide to share it with that person?
How important is trust between people?
part2.examiner_spoken: Part 2. Describe a time when you shared a secret with someone. Why did you decide to share it with that person? How important is trust between people?
part2.sample_answer: I remember sharing a secret with my closest friend at university, and it was one of those moments when I really understood what trust means. At that time, I had been offered a small scholarship to study abroad, but I had not told my family yet because I was worried about their reaction. I knew it was good news, but I also knew it could create pressure, so I wanted to think carefully before speaking to them. I decided to tell my best friend first, because she had always been honest, calm, and discreet. She never spread other people’s private information, and I felt completely safe with her. When I told her, she listened carefully, asked a few sensible questions, and then helped me see the situation more clearly. She didn’t judge me at all, which made me feel a lot better. After that, I had the confidence to explain everything to my family. Looking back, that experience showed me that trust is essential in any close relationship. If people trust each other, they can share worries, ask for advice, and be themselves. Without trust, even a friendship or family relationship can become weak and insecure.

part3.name: Part 3: Two-sided Discussion / Debate
part3.statement: Fast-food restaurants should display the number of calories in their meals.
arguments_for: helps people make an informed choice about what they eat
encourages restaurants to offer healthier options
could reduce obesity and diet-related illness
arguments_against: most customers ignore the numbers anyway
can create anxiety and guilt around food
calories say nothing about the real nutritional value
part3.examiner_spoken: Part 3. Look at the statement: Fast-food restaurants should display the number of calories in their meals. Use the arguments for and against.
part3.sample_answer: The question is whether fast-food restaurants should display the number of calories in their meals. I strongly believe they should, because this information can help people make more informed choices about what they eat. When customers can see the calorie content clearly, they are more likely to compare options and decide whether they really want a large burger, fries, and a sugary drink, or something lighter. In that sense, calorie labels can also push restaurants to think more seriously about health and to offer better alternatives. If this becomes normal, it could contribute to lower obesity levels and fewer diet-related illnesses in the long run. However, there are also some valid arguments against the idea. Some people simply ignore calorie numbers, so the labels may not change behaviour much. Others may become anxious or guilty about food, which is not healthy either, especially for people who already have a difficult relationship with eating. Another important point is that calories are only one part of the picture. A meal can be low in calories but still poor in nutrients, or high in calories but quite nutritious. My own view is that calorie information should definitely be shown, but it should be presented clearly and sensibly, without making people feel judged. It is a useful guide, not the whole answer, and it works best when people also learn about nutrition more broadly.
